CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up for anxiety management.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient was recently started on Buspar by Dr. Brown for anxiety and reports significant improvement. She experienced severe anxiety in November and December, with symptoms occurring during the day at work. During this time she was on Singulair (per Dr. Ward) and Progesterone. Dr. Ward noted that Singulair can cause anxiety; patient is uncertain if this was the etiology. She observed anxiety spiking the week before menses initially, then progressing to random episodes. She attributes some of her anxiety to work stress during the COVID-19 pandemic response, where she led delivery of COVID-19 test results to patients, and she felt guilt about experiencing anxiety while not working on the front lines. She discontinued Camila birth control due to significantly increased appetite and has since felt better with weight loss over the past 6 months.

Regarding breast health, she reports breast lumps that are smaller than previously but still present, with left-sided breast tenderness in the lower aspect similar to tenderness she experienced during breastfeeding with a clogged duct. She continues topical cream for vaginal itching and discomfort once weekly with good effect and needs a refill. She expresses concern about breast cancer risk given her age (approaching 40) and her mother's history of breast cancer diagnosed at approximately age 45. Last pap was in 2019 with negative results. She had an abnormal pap circa 2009 that required 6-month surveillance and subsequently normalized.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Reviewed. Positive for anxiety (improved on Buspar), breast tenderness and lumps (left-sided, smaller than previously), vaginal itching and discomfort (controlled with topical cream), and weight loss over past 6 months. Patient denies other issues.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Abnormal cervical cytology approximately 2009 (required 6-month surveillance, subsequently normalized)
Breast lumps/cysts
History of clogged duct during breastfeeding

MEDICATIONS
Buspar (new)
Progesterone (for menstrual regulation)
Singulair
Topical cream for vaginal itching and discomfort (used once weekly)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother: Breast cancer diagnosed at approximately age 45

SOCIAL HISTORY
Employment in healthcare setting involved in COVID-19 pandemic response, specifically leading delivery of COVID-19 test results to patients. COVID-19 vaccination status: Patient and son have received vaccine (son completed first dose); husband and daughter have vaccine hesitancy.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Lungs: Examined with normal breathing; no abnormalities noted
Neck: Small palpable nodules noted, smaller than previous examination; normal swallowing function
Breast: Left breast with increased density compared to right; tender in lower aspect; palpable lumps smaller than previously noted but still present
Pelvis: Normal appearance; itching/discomfort well-controlled with topical cream

RESULTS
Pap smear (2019): Negative/negative

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Anxiety: Currently well-controlled on Buspar. Continue current management.
2. Breast lumps/cysts: Referral placed to breast specialist for surveillance and evaluation. Specialist may perform in-office ultrasound and can manage procedures if needed. Specialist will contact patient within couple of business days to schedule appointment.
3. Cervical cytology: Repeat Pap smear due to history of abnormal results in 2009 and increased risk from stress and immunocompromise.
4. Vaginal itching/discomfort: Continue topical cream once weekly; provide refill.
5. Menstrual regulation: Continue Progesterone.
